Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl

Class AdHocToolRefusedException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl.AgentConnectorException
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl.AdHocToolRefusedException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class AdHocToolRefusedException extends AgentConnectorException
A tool call the agent may not make, phrased for the agent to read and act on.

The one exception an ad hoc tool hands to the model. "You already asked to end this scope", "that parameter must be a number", "wait, something is still running" — each is an answer, and a model that reads it can call again differently. The turn carries on.

Everything else a tool throws is a failure of the engine or of the deployment, and the model can do nothing with it. Passing an OptimisticLockingException on as a tool result told the model to carry on in a transaction already marked rollback-only: the commit failed at the end of the turn, the job ran three times, every model call was paid three times, and the incident carried the rollback and not the cause. Those are rethrown instead, and end the turn where they happened — see AgentConnectorImpl.toolFailure.

So the choice of type at a throw site is a decision about the reader: this class when the model is meant to read it, AgentConnectorException when a person is. A message naming toolClasses or a misplaced agent task belongs to the person — the model cannot move an activity in the diagram.
